title: Chronicle RCA: timeouts and tenant surge mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a multi-tenant traffic surge on 2025-02-09 hosted endpoints returned elevated 5xx rates and end-to-end request timeouts. Several high-value customers opened support escalations describing repeated retries increasing latency and causing downstream failures. This ticket captures the root cause analysis, the targeted production patch we are developing, temporary mitigations, and next steps for Dedicated/Private parity.

Scope and symptoms observed:
- Spike of 5xx errors (502/504) concentrated on routes backed by the L7 routing pool in us-west1 between 02:13–02:57 UTC.
- Increased connection timeouts reported by SDKs; mean p95 latency spiked from 120ms to 2.1s.
- Retry storms from customers amplified load; internal autoscaling lagged due to slow warm-up of GPU pools.
- KV cache thrashing on long-chat workloads caused memory pressure on some inference workers, leading to transient OOM restarts and connection resets.

Immediate mitigation applied (timeline):
- 02:40 UTC: throttled public client retries at edge (temporary bounded retry-window header introduced) to limit reissue rate. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7642
- 03:05 UTC: enabled lightweight circuit-breaker rule to route new requests to lower-latency fallback model variants for affected customers.
- 03:12 UTC: emergency patch to reduce max inflight requests per worker from 256 to 192 to reduce queue latency; rollback knob prepared.

Root cause hypothesis and evidence:
- Primary trigger: tenant-level burst of long-running generation requests that exceeded steady-state concurrency assumptions for our L7 routing + pooling code path.
- Secondary factor: retry amplification due to client-side optimistic retries without exponential backoff for streaming endpoints.
- Evidence: worker logs show KV cache eviction churn correlated with long sequence lengths; kube restarts tying to high RSS values; request traces show many duplicated request IDs within 10s windows. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood-infra/boards/INC-20250209-1

Planned permanent fixes (this ticket):
1) Implement bounded-retry-window and server-side deduplication for idempotent streamed requests (runtime + API layer). Estimate: 5 points.
2) Add tenant-level circuit-breaker with graduated cooldown + telemetry to automatically divert traffic to cheaper model variants when latency SLOs are threatened. Estimate: 8 points.
3) Improve KV cache eviction policy to be sequence-length aware and prefer stashing large KV pages to disk-backed cache on oversubscription. Estimate: 8 points.
4) Autoscaler warm-up tuning for GPU pools and a fast-slice prewarm path for short bursts. Estimate: 5 points.

Compatibility notes (Dedicated/Private):
- Dedicated: circuit-breaker config will be provided as an operator-managed policy; customers with reserved capacity can opt out but will receive warnings if the policy trips.
- Private: KMS and network constraints mean we will deliver a config bundle and runbook for on-prem teams; runtime changes require coordinated upgrade windows.

Rollout and safety plan:
- Deploy incremental changes behind feature flag targeting 5% of production traffic and internal stress tests for 48h.
- Monitor: token-level error breakdown, p95/p99 latency, inflight queue length, worker RSS, KV hit rate and eviction counts. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood-infra/boards/hosted-rca-19081
- Canary cutoff: automatic rollback if p99 latency increases by >15% or 5xx rate increases by >50% over baseline in the canary window.

Communication and customer follow-ups:
- CS provided a templated explanation and ETA to impacted customers on 2025-02-10 09:00 PST.
- Postmortem scheduled for 2025-02-19 with affected customers invited.

Acceptance criteria:
- 5xx rate for affected routes returns to baseline under a similar synthetic burst test.
- Retry amplification reduced as measured by duplicate-request rate falling >90% vs incident peak.
- No significant regression in latency for non-affected tenants.
- Runbook updated with mitigation steps and rollback instructions.
